title: 2024年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. Recent evidence points to drivers' limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse. A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint. It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately.

P2 One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products. But this is far from ideal. The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications. Further, most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms.

P3 The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software. And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware.

P4 "Warning fatigue" and distracted driving are also causes for concern. For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction. Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur.

P5 Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase. Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions. All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.

questions.q: What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction?
options: Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors.
Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people.
Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved.
There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction? 直接问研究告诉了我们 什么，答案必然是原文一句陈述的客观转述，不需要跨段推理。

【拆句】结构平铺直叙：主句是 What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction，from 引导的介宾短语限定信息来源，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。 46. What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction? A) Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors. B) Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people. C) Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved. D) There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles.

【定位】Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. 人车交互领域的研究表明，即便是为自动驾驶而设计的系统，也远远谈不上无差错。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 systems designed to automate driving ↔Automatic driving systems far from being error-proof ↔by no means immune to errors 预判要的是系统并非无差错，A 项 Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors 是对 systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof 的逐部分同义替换，无添加无减少，锁定 A。 B) 偷换概念 Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people 谈的是车被滥用，而题 干问的是研究发现，定位句结论是系统易出错，两者不在同一语义层；滥用确实在 system misuse 中提到但只是后续展开，并非首句的研究结论。 C) 无中生有 Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved 称厂商 对法律毫无意识，而原文 A recent study tackles the issue…from a legal viewpoint 只是说有研究从法律角度切入，从未说厂商不知情。 D) 偷换概念 There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles 把 研究结论说成人车交互本身遥不可及，而原文人车交互只是研究领域名，研究真正的发 现是系统易错，与是否能交互无关。 要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议存在什么问题? A) 无论老少,最终用户都觉得条款难以理解。 B) 大多数最终用户签署时根本不会费心阅读条款。 C) 许多人经常对条款的措辞感到困惑。 D) 大多数最终用户即使通读后也不理解这些条款。

questions.q: What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
options: End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret.
Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms.
Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms.
Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 询 问一个具体做法的问题所在，属于对原文局部反面描述的提取。

【拆句】结构清晰：What is the problem with… 主句问的是 problem，with 后跟动名词短语 requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements 作 problem 的定语，整体无 难点。 47. What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements? A) End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret. B) Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms. C) Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms. D) Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.

【定位】Further, most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. 更何况，大多数终端用户根本不读 EULA。2017 年的一项研究表明，91% 的人未读就同 意了。

【选项】A) 无中生有 End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret 说所有人都觉 得条款难以解读，但原文只说大家压根不读，从未说他们读了之后觉得难懂。 B) ✓ 正确 most end users don't read EULAs ↔ Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 91 percent of people agree to them without reading ↔Most end users 预判要的是签前不读，B 项 Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 正是这一行为的标准表述，与原文双句合并对应，锁定 B。 C) 偷换概念 Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms 说人们被措辞搞晕， 但原文 leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications 说的是对协议性质与含义的困惑，且这是协议信息不足的后果，不是 本题题干问的 EULA 整体的根本问题。 D) 与原文相反 Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through 隐含的 前提是用户把条款读完了，只是不懂；而原文 most end users don't read EULAs 的事 实是用户根本没读，两者前提相反。 当驾驶员遭受"警告疲劳"时会怎么做? A) 毫不拖延地保持汽车行驶。 B) 休息一会儿以避免疲劳驾驶。 C) 尽管反复警告也不采取行动。 D) 虽然疲劳但仍注意警告信息。

questions.q: What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"?
options: Waste no time keeping the car moving.
Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving.
Take no action despite repeated warnings.
Take note of the message though fatigued.
questions.explain:
【判型】What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"? 问的是在某情境下司 机会做出何种动作，属于对原文具体情境的事实提取。

【拆句】主句 What would drivers do 是常规疑问句，when 引导的时间状语从句 when they suffer from "warning fatigue" 限定情境，suffer from 意为遭受、深受其扰，无陷阱。 48. What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"? A) Waste no time keeping the car moving. B) Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving. C) Take no action despite repeated warnings. D) Take note of the message though fatigued.

【定位】For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. 举例来说，一名司机在接到接连不断的警告后心生厌烦，可能干脆决定无视这条信息。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Waste no time keeping the car moving 是 抓紧时间让车继续走，与原文 ignore the message 描述的不作为完全不是一回事。 B) 偷换概念 Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving 在谈疲劳驾驶要休息，但原文 "Warning fatigue" 指对警告厌烦，并非生理疲劳。 C) ✓ 正确 could decide to just ignore the message ↔Take no action despite repeated warnings 预判要的是无视警告这一行为，C 项 Take no action despite repeated warnings 把无 视＝不作为、反复警告＝重复警告两端都精准对位，锁定 C。 D) 与原文相反 Take note of the message though fatigued 是 虽然疲惫但仍留意警告，与原文 just ignore the message 完全相反。 作者如何看待继续要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议? A) 这可能无法保证发生事故时驾驶员的安全。 B) 这可能无法确保自动驾驶系统正常运行。 C) 这可能无法充分保护汽车制造商免受蓄意欺诈的指控。 D) 这可能无法为制造商提供充分的法律责任保护。

questions.q: What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
options: It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents.
It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly.
It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating.
It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 虽问作者看法，但锁定于 EULAs 这一局部做法，仍以一句明确表态句为答案 依据，属细节题。

【拆句】What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 中 think of 后接动名词 continuing，continuing 再接动词不定式 to ask buyers to sign…，是动名词+不定式连用的链式结构，意为对继续要求买家签 EULA 这件 事，作者怎么看。 49. What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? A) It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents. B) It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly. C) It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating. D) It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities.

【定位】Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur. 鉴于这些局限与担忧，即使继续推行这种取得同意的方式，万一系统发生故障或事故发生， 它也很可能无法在法律责任上充分保护汽车制造商。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents 谈的是事 故中司机的安全保障，但原文 protect automakers from their legal liability 谈的是保 护厂商免于法律责任，对象与内容都错位。 B) 偷换概念 It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly 谈的是 系统能否正常运行，但原文谈的是法律层面对厂商的保护，二者根本不是一回事。 C) 偷换概念 It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating 谈的是免于被指故意欺诈，但原文 legal liability 仅指法律责任，未涉及 deliberate cheating 故意欺诈这一更窄、更带主观恶意的范畴。 D) ✓ 正确 it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability ↔ It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities automakers ↔manufacturers 预判要的是不能充分保护厂商的法律责任，D 项 It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities 与定位句逐字对 位，锁定 D。 应该做什么来帮助驾驶员充分了解系统的功能和局限性? A) 培训他们成为车辆自动化方面的专家。 B) 通过培训使他们熟悉这些系统。 C) 拓宽他们对事故预防机制的了解。 D) 便利他们获取销售方提供的信息。

questions.q: What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations?
options: Training them to be experts in vehicle automation.
Familiarizing them with the systems through training.
Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms.
Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations? 直接问该做什么以达成目的，属于对原文解决方案句的提取。

【拆句】主句 What should be done 是被动疑问句，to help 引导的不定式作目的状语，help drivers 后接动词原形 fully understand…，整句意思是：为帮司机充分理解系统能力与局 限，应该做什么。 50. What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations? A) Training them to be experts in vehicle automation. B) Familiarizing them with the systems through training. C) Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms. D) Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller.

【定位】Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. 针对自动驾驶汽车的司机培训，能够帮助确保司机充分了解系统的能力与局限。

【选项】A) 过度推断 Training them to be experts in vehicle automation 把目标拔到成为车辆自动化领域 专家的高度，而原文只要求 fully understand system capabilities and limitations，是 理解层级而非专家层级。 B) ✓ 正确 Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations ↔Familiarizing them with the systems through training fully understand system capabilities and limitations ↔Familiarizing them with the systems 预判要的是通过培训让司机熟悉系统，B 项 Familiarizing them with the systems through training 与定位句双层等值，锁定 B。 C) 无中生有 Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms 谈的是扩大防事 故机制的知识面，但原文谈的是理解系统的能力与局限，accident-prevention mechanisms 在文中并未出现。 D) 与原文相反 Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller 主张方便司机获 取卖家信息，但原文 even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions 明确指出哪怕依赖卖家信息也无法解答许多问题， 二者方向相反。
